questions.solution:
The given sentence is an example of reported speech. Reported speech is speech which tells you what someone said but does not use the person's actual words.

Reported speech is always in past form.

So, 'has', and 'will' in options (a) and (b) make them incorrect.

In option (c), it is in the perfect conditional tense. We use it for something that might have happened in the past. Since the given sentence is not conditional, option (c) is incorrect.

So, the underlined phrase can be replaced with option (d) 'he had seen the picture'.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

The correct sentence is: Abu said that he had seen the picture.

The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['be' in this sentence] and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs and they should be used correctly as stated below.

Some of the modal verbs are: Can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of such a sentence in Active voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

For example:

This can be done by you. (Passive Voice)

You can do this. (Active Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

For example:

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Perfect tense. There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

· Tense remains same

· Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

· Past perfect changes to Simple Past

In these cases, we go by the options.

As per the given options, the given indirect from in past perfect tense is to be changed to the past simple tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

The reporting verb may remain the same or be changed to 'said'.

'How I had' is changed to 'how did you'

The pronoun 'his' is changed to 'my'.

'Did' is always followed by the base verb. So, option (b) is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): "How did you persuade my sister?" Shyam asked me.

questions.solution:
We use until as a subordinating conjunction to connect an action or an event to a point in time. Example: Let's wait here until the rain stops.

So, 'unless' should be replaced with 'until'.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

'Unless' is similar in meaning to 'if not' and can be used instead of 'if not' in certain types of conditional sentences.

The correct sentence is: One can never imagine how hot it gets in Delhi until one doesn't go there in person.

Q. Wular Lake is also said to be a remnant of Satisar Lake that existed in ancient times.

R. This lake has a small island in its centre called the 'Zaina Lank'.

'RS' is a pair that informs about the small island that is there in the centre of the lake, and whom it was built by is mentioned in S.

'Also' in Q implies that it gives an additional fact about Wular Lake.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['being' in the given sentence] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Continuous.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): A few men were helping the wounded man.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. The continuous P. the growing sales of sneakers Q. dominance of the athleisure trend R. along with the pursuit of comfort S. has had a significant impact on
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

The continuous

P. the growing sales of sneakers

Q. dominance of the athleisure trend

R. along with the pursuit of comfort

S. has had a significant impact on
questions.solution:
The adjective 'continuous' will be followed by a noun. Only part Q contains the noun 'dominance'. So, the first phrase after 'the continuous' would be Q.

Only two options have 'Q' at the start of the sequence.

Part 'S' ends with the preposition 'on'.

So, it cannot come in the end.

'S' comes after 'Q' and implies that there is some significant impact of the 'athleisure trend'.

PR forms a pair and mentions the things impacted by the athleisure trend.

So, the correct order is QSPR.

Hence, the correct sentence after rearrangement is: The continuous dominance of the athleisure trend has had a significant impact on the growing sales of sneakers along with the pursuit of comfort.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.
